name: Sprocket
text: Decide to run a 7-day hard decay on every prompt in the system. This forces stale prompts to expire, keeping the system lean and current. The trade-off is losing some prompts that might still be useful but haven’t been used recently—accept that risk to avoid clutter and confusion.

name: Gauge
text: A 7-day hard decay guarantees losing prompts that only fire in rare edge cases—those you can’t afford to lose. Instead, run a 30-day sliding decay with a manual review queue: stale prompts auto-expire unless tagged "keep," forcing active curation without blind deletion. Settle it by auditing the last 90 days of prompt usage to quantify the real loss.

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Replace every prompt in the system with a 7-day hard decay rule. Old prompts lose access after 7 days unless explicitly renewed, cutting clutter and forcing fresh reviews. Trade-off: we lose some context from older prompts, but we gain faster iteration and cleaner routing.

name: Gauge
text: A 7-day hard decay risks losing context critical for routing—some prompts only fire in rare edge cases where the user’s intent isn’t obvious. A better alternative is a sliding decay tied to prompt usage, not time, so stale but still-relevant prompts stay accessible until proven irrelevant. Settle it by measuring how often edge-case prompts fail to route after the change.

name: Gauge
text: A 7-day hard decay doesn’t just lose edge-case context—it guarantees misrouting for users who rely on those rare prompts, because the system can’t distinguish between "stale" and "critical." A better alternative is a usage-based sliding decay with a manual override for high-value prompts, so we keep what matters without manual renewal. Settle it by testing both rules on a 30-day sample of real user traffic and measuring misroute rates.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Adopt a hybrid decay system—7-day hard decay for prompts under 100 uses, 14-day rolling decay with 10% floor for all others, plus manual override for high-value prompts.

Result: A prompt decay system that balances freshness with critical context retention, owned by the routing team lead.
